body: ## Summary Supersedes #6743. That PR is stacked on #6735, which was closed without merging, and it conflicts with main. Most of it is already covered on main: | Part of #6743 | Status on main | |---|---| | Dirty-propagation frontier | Covered by #7312: `Field.__set__` calls `_mark_dirty((name,))`, so a write walks only the dependents of the var that changed. | | `_interval_computed_vars` | Covered by #7025 (`_interval_computed_var_names`). | | Return-type check on recompute only | **This PR.** | | Shallow type check in prod | **This PR.** | | Per-field `MutableProxy` cache | Left out. See below. | ### Changes 1. **A cached computed var checks its return type only when it recomputes** (sync and async). Before, every read ran `_check_deprecated_return_type` with `nested=1`, even on a cache hit, in every mode. 2. **In prod mode, state var assignments and computed var results check only the outer type** (`nested=0`). The check only logs an error. Dev mode keeps the element check. The mode is read from `REFLEX_ENV_MODE` on each call, with an exact comparison that matches the canonical enum parser. `environment.REFLEX_ENV_MODE.get()` costs about 2.4 µs, too much for every write. Scalar values never reach this check, because `_plain_types` short-circuits first. ### Measurements Micro-benchmarks, in-process, py3.14, median of 15: | | main | this PR | |---|---|---| | Read a cached computed var returning about 250 dicts (any mode) | 321 µs | 0.43 µs | | Assign a list of 500 dicts (prod) | 248 µs | 2.6 µs | | Assign a list of 500 dicts (dev) | 247 µs | 248 µs | | Assign an `int` (prod) | 2.5 µs | 2.6 µs | End to end, over a websocket: prod backend, one granian worker, server and client on separate pinned cores. There were 7 interleaved rounds of 2,000 serial events (600 for the reassign). Values are the median and [min–max] of the 7 rounds: | Handler | main p50 RTT | this PR p50 RTT | CPU per event | |---|---|---|---| | Reassign a 500-row list + dependent computed var | 2651 [2541–3099] µs | 2156 [2114–2179] µs | **−18%**, 7/7 rounds | | `count += 1`, list append, nested mutation, substate | — | — | no change expected. Moves of ±5–12% in both directions are run-to-run noise, because this diff does not touch those paths. | The win shows only for handlers that assign large containers or read cached computed vars. Typical scalar and in-place mutation events do not change. ### Not included: the proxy cache In the same A/B, caching the top-level `MutableProxy` per field saved about 1.1 µs per read. It gave −13% only in a handler that read `self.items` 50 times, and nothing on append or nested mutation. It also changes behavior: two reads return the same proxy, so overlapping `async with self.items` blocks now raise `RuntimeError: Mutable proxy is already in an async context`. It also needs an extra slot and an extra `pop` on every tracked write. Background tasks get no benefit, because `StateProxy` re-wraps on every read. ## Tests - New tests in `tests/units/reflex_base/vars/test_base.py` fail on main and pass here: - A sync or async cached computed var checks its return type once per recompute. - The element-type error is logged in dev and not in prod. - The outer-type error is logged in both modes. - `uv run pytest tests/units`: 11043 passed. - ruff, pyright and pre-commit are clean.
title: perf: skip redundant state var type checks on the hot path
